For years, many women have known this condition as PCOS. But now, the term PMOS (PolyMetabolic Ovary Syndrome) is being discussed because experts believe it explains the condition better 👀

Why? Because it’s not only about the ovaries.

This condition can affect hormones, blood sugar levels, weight, skin, hair health, metabolism, fertility, and overall health.

Common signs can include:  
✨ Irregular or missed periods  
✨ Weight gain or difficulty losing weight  
✨ Acne or oily skin  
✨ Excess facial or body hair  
✨ Hair thinning or hair fall  
✨ Tiredness or low energy  
✨ Cravings or increased hunger  
✨ Dark skin patches around the neck or underarms  
✨ Difficulty getting pregnant for some women

The idea behind PMOS is to help women understand that this condition can affect the whole body — not just the ovaries. 

The goal? Better understanding earlier support, and more whole body care ❤️
